$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file.
purpose: T1 replaces 24 hand-written `api/v1` route literals — 23 source lines across
20 controller files, identical on the frozen origin/main oracle and on v1 —
with ONE expression of the version: setGlobalPrefix("api") +
enableVersioning({ type: URI, defaultVersion: "1" }), declared in
apps/agent/src/http/api-surface.ts and installed by main.ts.
THE ONE CLAIM THAT MATTERS IS NEGATIVE: not one of the 300 REST operations
moved. A route that silently moves is a broken client, and 'silently' is the
operative word — every entry below is a way the surface could move while a
gate stayed green, run live to see which gate actually goes red.
THREE MECHANISMS COMPOSE THE PATHS, AND THEY SHARE NOTHING:
(1) apps/agent/scripts/generate-control-plane.mjs — STATIC, from the
TypeScript AST, reading the prefix/version/exclusion constants out of
api-surface.ts and emitting operation-manifest.generated.json.
(2) apps/agent/src/http/api-surface.test.ts — RUNTIME: the real controllers
in a real Nest application, the same applyApiSurface main.ts calls, and
the route table read back out of Express.
(3) scripts/rest-census-independent.mjs — globs the controller files and
reconciles decorator counts against the manifest without the
generator's allowlist.
M06 IS THE ENTRY THIS LEDGER EXISTS FOR. It moves 51 real routes and leaves
BOTH static enumerators at exit 0. Only the runtime probe sees it. Without
that entry, 'the generated manifest did not change' would be an argument
about an AST rather than about a server.
NOTHING HERE NEEDS A DATABASE, A CONTAINER OR A DOCKER DAEMON. Every case is
a file edit plus one node or vitest process.
procedure: PROVE GREEN FIRST. The unmutated tree was run green before and after every
entry below. An entry whose suite was already red proves nothing, and a
'kill' with no named failing line is VACUOUS — see `declared` for the two
places this ledger refuses to claim a kill it did not watch.
For one entry: apply `to` to `file`, run `command`, confirm the NAMED line
or case in `kills` appears and the process exits non-zero. Then revert and
`file` is REPOSITORY-relative. `control` records a command that stayed GREEN
under the same mutation, which is what makes the killing gate load-bearing
rather than one of several redundant copies.

declared.what: No mutation makes DROPPING `version: API_VERSION` from a v1 controller fail.
declared.why: Verified live, not assumed: rewriting `@Controller({ path: "agent/skills", version: API_VERSION })` to `@Controller("agent/skills")` leaves `generate-control-plane --check` at exit 0 and all 8 route-identity cases green. That is the DESIGN, not a gap — `defaultVersion: "1"` is the floor, so a controller that says nothing about the version is v1, and the only way to leave the versioned surface is an explicit VERSION_NEUTRAL, which M05 does catch. A gate that fired here would be asserting a redundant decorator rather than a URL.

declared.what: No mutation exercises apps/webapp, which still calls `/api/v1/agent/...` as literal strings in 84 BFF route files.
declared.why: Those are HTTP CLIENT paths over the wire to a separate process, not Nest route declarations, and the same is true of the ~30 pathname comparisons in `apps/agent/src/auth/scope.guard.ts` and the UNAUTH_BODY_CAPS table in main.ts. They are deliberately left literal: the claim of this tranche is that the wire paths do not move, and a guard that kept matching the literal it always matched is an independent witness to that. Deriving them from API_VERSION would make the guard agree with the router BY CONSTRUCTION. WIN-267's REST-literal measurement is decorator-scoped (contract-map.mjs measureApiV1Literals) and reports 0 across apps/, packages/ and internal-packages/.

declared.what: The route-identity probe does not run the controllers' constructor injection.
declared.why: Vitest transforms with esbuild, which does not implement emitDecoratorMetadata, so `design:paramtypes` is absent and Nest cannot resolve a constructor argument in this repository with or without T1. The probe erases the injection metadata and runs Nest in preview mode, which never calls a constructor or a lifecycle hook. The metadata under test — PATH_METADATA, VERSION_METADATA and the HTTP-method decorators — is untouched, and erasing any of it turns every case in the suite red. This is stated rather than glossed because it is the one respect in which the probe is not the production process.
